message.content:
MonoDreams currently only builds for desktop (Windows, MacOS, and Linux), the goal of this session is to enable targeting Web Browsers (we'll focus on Chrome latest). The chosen path is to use the KNI library. First, get yourself familiar with KNI:
 - https://github.com/kniengine/kni
 - https://darkgenesis.zenithmoon.com/monogame-on-the-web-No-really!.html
 - https://blog.nkast.gr/post/what-s-new-in-kni-v4-02
Second, plan on how to enable devs using MonoDreams to easily target the Web and have games that can run specifically on one platform or be multi-platform (desktop + web).

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)

- Before making schema changes, use `list_tables` to understand the existing structure
- When debugging issues, start with `get_logs` and `get_advisors` before making changes
- Use `get_project_url` and `get_publishable_api_key` when helping users configure client-side integrations

Substitui o plan mode interativo; usada isoladamente ou como etapa 1 do /implement.

Round 1 em largura, rounds seguintes em profundidade (validador + fix-diff + re-enumeração); repete até exaustão — 0 High/Blocker em round de largura com enumeração seca (cap 5 rounds) — + uma rodada final para Medium/Low.

# KNI Game Framework Summary

## What is KNI?

"KNI is a simple and powerful .NET framework for creating games for desktop PCs, Mobile devices, Virtual Reality headsets and the Web, using dotnet framework & the C# programming language." It represents an open-source reimplementation of Microsoft's discontinued XNA Framework, building upon MonoGame and XNA Touch as its foundation.

## Relationship to MonoGame/XNA

KNI serves as a derivative work of the MonoGame project, maintaining API compatibility with XNA while modernizing the framework. The project acknowledges its roots by stating it's "a derivative of MonoGame & XNA Touch" and provides XNA samples ported to KNI through a separate repository.

## Supported Platforms

The framework targets an extensive platform range:
- **Desktop**: Windows (OpenGL & DirectX11), macOS, Linux
- **Mobile**: Android 6.0+, iOS 10.0+
- **VR/AR**: Oculus VR, Google Cardboard
- **Web**: "Web Browsers & WebXR (WebGL)" including Blazor support

## Web Development with KNI

Projects targeting web platforms use the Blazor.GL solution, with the framework supporting WebGL rendering. This enables developers to build web-based games using the same C# codebase as desktop applications, leveraging WASM (WebAssembly) capabilities through the .NET runtime.

## Project Structure & Tools

KNI employs:
- **Project SDK**: Standard .NET project files per platform
- **Content Pipeline**: MGCB (MonoGame Content Builder) for asset processing
- **Effect Compiler**: KNIFXC for shader compilation
- **GUI Tool**: Pipeline-editor for visual content processing

## Key Differences from MonoGame

While maintaining XNA compatibility, KNI diverges by providing dedicated platform-specific solutions (.sln files) for each target environment rather than a unified approach, enabling optimized implementations for web, VR, and mobile platforms while preserving the familiar XNA API surface.

# Running MonoGame on the Web with KNI

## Step-by-Step Process

1. **Install KNI SDK**: Download and run the KNI Engine installer (e.g., KniSdkSetup3.9.9001.exe) which automatically installs Visual Studio 2022 project templates
2. **Create Web Project**: Use the "KNI Web Browser Template" in Visual Studio to scaffold a new project
3. **Configure Game Class**: Rename or keep the default `KNIBrowserGame.cs` class, ensuring `Index.razor.cs` references the correct class name
4. **Build & Test**: Run locally—a web browser launches with your game running via Blazor
5. **Deploy to GitHub Pages**: Configure workflow permissions, enable GitHub Pages with "GitHub Actions" source, and commit a YAML deployment workflow

## Technical Requirements

**NuGet & Dependencies**: KNI libraries are published on NuGet, though project templates still require Visual Studio installation for web support.

**Project Structure**:
- `Program.cs`: Custom web initialization (do not modify)
- `KNIBrowserGame.cs`: Your main game logic (equivalent to Game1.cs)
- `Index.razor`: Web initialization page with renderable canvas
- `Index.razor.cs`: C# code-behind for web setup
- `wwwroot/`: Deployable web folder

## BlazorGL Platform

The article references `#if !BLAZORGL` preprocessor directives, indicating BlazorGL is the web platform identifier. This allows conditional compilation to exclude unsupported features from web builds.

## Game Code Structure

Desktop and web implementations share the same codebase fundamentally. However, web versions require platform-specific handling:

```
#if !BLAZORGL
    // Desktop-only code (GamePad input, etc.)
#endif
```

## Key Limitations & Gotchas

- **Unsupported Features**: GamePad and touchscreen input, complex shaders, file access restrictions
- **Visual Studio Template Issues**: May require restart or running `devenv /updateConfiguration`
- **csproj Configuration**: Remove `<Import Project="$(MSBuildExtensionsPath)\MonoGame\v3.0\MonoGame.Content.Builder17.targets" />` for automated builds (local builds tolerate it)
- **Debugging**: Browser F12 developer tools provide error diagnostics since Visual Studio debugging doesn't extend to web execution
- **Performance**: "The Web is NOT your desktop"—expect limitations compared to native builds

## Content Pipeline

Projects use KNI's MGCB editor (not Visual Studio's) for the `KNIBrowserContent.mgcb` file, handling asset compilation for web deployment.

content.content:
# KNI v4.02 Summary

## Key Features & Improvements

**Graphics Backends**: SharpDX upgraded to 4.2.0, OpenAL now includes OBOE integration for improved audio performance, and a new KNIFX shader format replaces legacy MGFX v09.

**Platform-Specific Enhancements**:
- **Android**: Supports 16K page-aligned binaries for Android 15+ compliance; adds mouse input and SetCursor() support
- **Windows**: DirectX keyboard input enabled by default in WinForms/UWP contexts
- **SDL2**: MediaPlayer looped playback now repeats "seamlessly without silent gaps"

## Web/WASM/Blazor Advances

Blazor.GL substantially expanded with instanced rendering via DrawInstancedPrimitives(), enabling "40K Instances @60fps" in browser samples. Additional web capabilities include GameWindow.OnTextInput, Mouse.SetCursor(), WebAudio panning, float32 audio support, DynamicSoundEffectInstance streaming, and live Microphone input capture.

## Pipeline & Content Changes

The Pipeline Editor includes NuGet resolution feedback, sorted file paths, and writes only modified processor parameters. Media transcoding now targets .WMA/.MP3 for audio and .WMV/.WebM for video across platforms.

## Cross-Platform Guidance

The changelog emphasizes migration documentation and suggests consulting "migrate to v4.2" resources. Shader preprocessor defines (__KNIFX__, __GL__, __GLES__) support conditional platform compilation, facilitating shared code strategies.

## Comprehensive Report: MonoDreams CLI and Module Distribution System

I've thoroughly explored the MonoDreams codebase. Here's my detailed mapping of the CLI, module manifest system, and distribution mechanism:

---

### 1. MonoDreams.Cli Project Structure and Commands

**File Path:** `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/.worktrees/feat/kni/MonoDreams.Cli/`

The CLI is a single .NET 8.0 console application using `System.CommandLine` for command parsing. It exposes three commands:

#### **a) `monodreams init <name> [--dir <path>]`**
- **Implementation:** `InitCommand.cs` → `Runner.RunInitAsync()`
- **Flow:**
  1. Validates project name (letters/digits/underscore/dash, must start with letter)
  2. Calls `ProjectScaffolder.Scaffold()` to generate initial project structure:
     - Creates `.csproj` file with hardcoded template (`OutputType=WinExe`, `TargetFramework=net8.0`)
     - Generates `Program.cs` with a basic `Game` class inheriting from `Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Game`
     - Creates `app.manifest` (Windows app manifest)
     - Creates `.gitignore` (bin/, obj/, debug/, *.user)
  3. Loads the registry and auto-installs the `foundation` module
  4. Creates `monodreams.json` state file with installed modules list
  5. Prints post-install notes from foundation module

**Generated Project Files:**
```
<projectname>/
  ├── <projectname>.csproj  (WinExe, net8.0, hardcoded template)
  ├── Program.cs            (Game class scaffold)
  ├── app.manifest          (Windows manifest)
  ├── .gitignore
  ├── monodreams.json       (state tracking)
  └── MonoDreams/
      └── foundation/       (copied from registry)
          ├── *.cs files
          └── docs/
```

#### **b) `monodreams add <modules...> [--preset <name>] [--project <dir>] [--dry-run]`**
- **Implementation:** `AddCommand.cs` → `Runner.RunAddAsync()`
- **Flow:**
  1. Loads the registry and project's `monodreams.json` state
  2. Accepts either individual module names or a preset name
  3. Calls `DependencyResolver.Resolve()` to compute transitive closure of dependencies
  4. For each resolved module:
     - Calls `Installer.Apply(manifest)` which:
       - Enumerates all files in the module directory (except `module.json`)
       - Copies files preserving relative paths from `MonoDreams/<module>/` to user's project
       - Edits the project's `.csproj` via `CsprojEditor.ApplyModule()` to inject NuGet references and MSBuild properties
       - Appends MGCB (content pipeline) entries via `MgcbEditor.ApplyModule()` if present
  5. Updates `monodreams.json` with newly installed modules
  6. Prints post-install notes from each module

#### **c) `monodreams list [--verbose | -v]`**
- **Implementation:** `ListCommand.cs` → `Runner.RunList()`
- **Output:** Lists all available modules and presets, optionally showing dependencies, NuGet packages, and premises references

**CLI Project Files:**
```
MonoDreams.Cli/
├── Program.cs              (entry point, sets up root command)
├── MonoDreams.Cli.csproj   (PackAsTool: true, ToolCommandName: monodreams)
├── Commands/
│   ├── InitCommand.cs
│   ├── AddCommand.cs
│   ├── ListCommand.cs
│   └── Runner.cs           (all command logic)
├── Installer/
│   ├── ProjectScaffolder.cs (writes .csproj, Program.cs, app.manifest, .gitignore)
│   ├── Installer.cs         (orchestrates file copy + csproj/mgcb editing)
│   ├── CsprojEditor.cs      (XDocument manipulation for NuGet + properties)
│   └── MgcbEditor.cs        (appends lines to Content.mgcb)
├── Manifest/
│   ├── ModuleManifest.cs    (JSON model for module.json)
│   ├── Registry.cs          (loads manifests from filesystem or bundled)
│   ├── RegistryIndex.cs     (list structure)
│   └── StateFile.cs         (monodreams.json model)
└── Resolver/
    └── DependencyResolver.cs (depth-first topological sort)
```

---

### 2. Module Manifest System

**Schema File:** `/Users/rodrigooliveira/git/roo-oliv/monodreams/.worktrees/feat/kni/MonoDreams/module.schema.json`

**Manifest Structure** (required fields, then optional):

| Field | Type | Required | Purpose |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `name` | string (kebab-case) | YES | Module identifier, must match directory name |
| `description` | string (≤120 chars) | YES | One-line summary shown by `monodreams list` |
| `dependencies` | array of strings | NO | Other modules required (transitive); resolved at install time |
| `nugetDependencies` | array of objects | NO | NuGet packages to inject into user's .csproj |
| `csprojProperties` | object (key-value) | NO | MSBuild properties appended to csproj PropertyGroup |
| `files` | array of objects | NO | Override implicit file list (source/destination/kind mappings) |
| `mgcbEntries` | array of strings | NO | Lines appended to Content/Content.mgcb for content pipeline |
| `postInstallNotes` | string (markdown) | NO | Terminal output after install (wiring instructions) |
| `agentsMd` | string (path) | NO | Path to AGENTS.md snippet appended to user's project AGENTS.md |
| `premisesRef` | string (path) | NO | Reference to docs/premises.md for module invariants |
| `demo` | object | NO | Optional runnable demo (entry class, description, extra dependencies) |

**File Copy Convention:**
- By default, **every file** in `MonoDreams/<module>/` (except `module.json`) is copied to the user's project at the same relative path
- Namespaces are file-path independent in C#, so `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` → user's `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` with namespace `MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`
- If a module needs files from outside its directory, it explicitly lists them in `files[].source/destination`

**Module Directory Layout Example:**
```
MonoDreams/
├── module.schema.json       (JSON Schema for all manifests)
├── presets.json             (curated module combinations)
├── MODULES.md               (docs, this file)
├── MonoDreams.csproj        (engine project, references all modules via glob)
├── foundation/              (required base)
│   ├── module.json
│   ├── Screen/
│   │   ├── ScreenController.cs
│   │   └── IGameScreen.cs
│   ├── System/
│   ├── Component/
│   ├── Input/
│   ├── Hierarchy/
│   ├── Transform/
│   ├── Logger/
│   ├── Replay/
│   └── docs/
│       └── premises.md
├── rendering/
│   ├── module.json
│   ├── Draw/
│   ├── Camera/
│   ├── Culling/
│   ├── MasterRenderSystem.cs
│   └── ...
├── ui/
│   ├── module.json
│   ├── Layout/
│   │   ├── AutoLayoutSystem.cs
│   │   ├── AutoLayoutBuilder.cs
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── demo/                (excluded from core, included with --with-demo)
│   │   └── ...
│   └── ...
├── camera/
│   ├── module.json          (has demo field)
│   ├── Component/
│   ├── System/
│   ├── demo/
│   │   └── CameraDemoScreen.cs
│   └── ...
└── ... (11 more modules)
```

**Example Manifest: `foundation/module.json`**
```json
{
  "name": "foundation",
  "description": "Required base: ECS world, screen controller, hierarchy/transform, input, replay, logger",
  "dependencies": [],
  "nugetDependencies": [
    { "id": "MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL", "version": "3.8.4" },
    { "id": "DefaultEcs", "version": "0.18.0-beta01" }
  ],
  "csprojProperties": {},
  "mgcbEntries": [],
  "postInstallNotes": "## foundation installed\n\nYour project now has...",
  "premisesRef": "docs/premises.md"
}
```

**Example Manifest with Complex Wiring: `dialogue/module.json`**
```json
{
  "name": "dialogue",
  "description": "YarnSpinner dialogue with content pipeline importer...",
  "dependencies": ["rendering-text", "ui"],
  "nugetDependencies": [
    { "id": "YarnSpinner", "version": "3.0.2" },
    { "id": "YarnSpinner.Compiler", "version": "3.0.2" },
    { "id": "CsvHelper", "version": "31.0.4" }
  ],
  "csprojProperties": {
    "CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies": "true",
    "EnableDynamicLoading": "true",
    "GenerateRuntimeConfigurationFiles": "true"
  },
  "mgcbEntries": [
    "/importer:YarnSpinnerImporter",
    "/processor:YarnSpinnerProcessor"
  ],
  "postInstallNotes": "## dialogue installed\n\n**Content pipeline.** Your project DLL must be referenced by MGCB...",
  "premisesRef": "docs/premises.md"
}
```

---

### 3. How `monodreams add <module>` Works

**File:** `MonoDreams.Cli/Installer/Installer.cs`

**Step-by-step flow for `monodreams add rendering camera collision`:**

1. **Dependency Resolution** (`DependencyResolver.cs`):
   - Loads manifest for each requested module
   - Performs depth-first traversal of the dependency graph
   - Topologically sorts the result (dependencies first)
   - Skips any module already in `monodreams.json`
   - Result for above: `["rendering", "camera", "collision"]` (rendering must be installed before camera)

2. **File Enumeration** (`Installer.EnumerateFiles()`):
   - If manifest has explicit `files[]`, use that
   - Otherwise, walk `MonoDreams/<module>/` recursively, collecting all files except `module.json`
   - Determine `kind` (code, asset, tool) based on file extension
   - Return list of `FileEntry{source, destination, kind}`

3. **File Copy** (`Installer.Apply()`):
   ```csharp
   foreach (var file in EnumerateFiles(manifest))
   {
       var src = Path.Combine(registry.EngineRoot, file.Source);
       var dst = Path.Combine(projectDir, file.Destination);
       Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(dst)!);
       File.Copy(src, dst, overwrite: true);
   }
   ```

4. **Csproj Editing** (`CsprojEditor.ApplyModule()`):
   - Loads user's `.csproj` as XDocument
   - If module has `nugetDependencies`, creates/gets `<ItemGroup Label="MonoDreams.Cli managed">` and adds `<PackageReference>` entries
   - If module has `csprojProperties`, creates/gets `<PropertyGroup Label="MonoDreams.Cli managed">` and adds properties
   - Saves modified XDocument back to disk

5. **MGCB Editing** (`MgcbEditor.ApplyModule()`):
   - If `Content/Content.mgcb` exists and module has `mgcbEntries`:
     - Appends a marker comment: `# --- <module-name> (managed by monodreams-cli) ---`
     - Appends each entry
   - Idempotent: checks for marker to avoid duplication

6. **State Update** (`StateFile.Save()`):
   - Appends module names to `monodreams.json` modules list
   - Updates `updatedAt` timestamp

**Key Design:** No circular dependencies allowed; resolver throws on cycle detection.

---

### 4. Search for Existing Platform/Target/Desktop/Web References

**Grep Results:**
```bash
grep -r "platform|target|desktop|web|wasm" /MonoDreams.Cli --include="*.cs" --include="*.json" --include="*.md"
# NO MATCHES
```

**However, there is one hardcoded platform decision:**

In `ProjectScaffolder.cs`:
```csharp
private static void WriteCsproj(string projectDir, string projectName)
{
    var path = Path.Combine(projectDir, $"{projectName}.csproj");
    File.WriteAllText(path, $"""
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>          // <-- Desktop-only
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework> // <-- No multi-target
    <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <PublishReadyToRun>false</PublishReadyToRun>
    <TieredCompilation>false</TieredCompilation>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

And in `foundation/module.json`:
```json
"nugetDependencies": [
  { "id": "MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL", "version": "3.8.4" }  // <-- Desktop GL
]
```

**Current State:**
- No notion of "target platform" anywhere in the manifest schema
- No flags or conditionals in CLI commands for platform selection
- All scaffolded projects are `WinExe` targeting `net8.0`
- Foundation hardcodes `MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` (desktop-only)

---

### 5. Project Templates and Scaffolding

**Template Generation:** All templates are **embedded in the CLI as strings** in `ProjectScaffolder.cs`

**Generated on `monodreams init`:**

1. **`.csproj` template** (lines 17–30 of ProjectScaffolder.cs):
   ```xml
   <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
     <PropertyGroup>
       <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>
       <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
       <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
       <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
       <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
       <PublishReadyToRun>false</PublishReadyToRun>
       <TieredCompilation>false</TieredCompilation>
     </PropertyGroup>
   </Project>
   ```

2. **`Program.cs` template** (lines 33–70):
   ```csharp
   using Microsoft.Xna.Framework;
   using Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics;

   namespace {projectName};

   public class {projectName}Game : Game
   {
       private readonly GraphicsDeviceManager _graphics;

       public {projectName}Game()
       {
           _graphics = new GraphicsDeviceManager(this);
           IsMouseVisible = true;
       }

       protected override void Update(GameTime gameTime)
       {
           base.Update(gameTime);
       }

       protected override void Draw(GameTime gameTime)
       {
           GraphicsDevice.Clear(Color.CornflowerBlue);
           base.Draw(gameTime);
       }

       public static void Main()
       {
           using var game = new {projectName}Game();
           game.Run();
       }
   }
   ```

3. **`app.manifest`** (lines 73–82):
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
   <assembly manifestVersion="1.0" xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v1">
     <assemblyIdentity version="1.0.0.0" name="MonoGame.App"/>
   </assembly>
   ```

4. **`.gitignore`** (lines 85–94):
   ```
   bin/
   obj/
   debug/
   *.user
   ```

**No external template files exist.** Everything is C# string literals in `ProjectScaffolder.cs`.

---

### 6. Module Dependency Graph

**13 modules total**, organized in a DAG:

```
foundation (root, no deps)
├── rendering
│   ├── rendering-text
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug (+ collision soft-coupling)
│   ├── level-ldtk (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui
│       └── dialogue (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision (+ physics soft-coupling)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

**Presets** (curated module combinations in `presets.json`):
- `ldtk-platformer` — full 2D platformer with LDtk levels, dialogue, UI
- `blender-platformer` — same but with Blender-exported levels
- `infinite-runner` — procedural runner (no level files, minimal UI)

---

### 7. State Tracking

**File:** `monodreams.json` (generated in project root after `init`)

```json
{
  "schema": "https://monodreams.dev/state.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "modules": ["foundation", "rendering", "camera"],
  "createdAt": "2025-06-21T12:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-06-21T12:05:00Z"
}
```

This file is used by `add` to skip already-installed modules and prevent redundant copies.

---

### 8. Registry Loading

**File:** `Registry.cs`

The registry can come from three sources (in priority order):
1. **Explicit path:** `--registry <path>` flag
2. **Repo root:** If run from within the engine repo (detected by presence of `MonoDreams/` with `module.json` files)
3. **Bundled:** Embedded in the CLI tool during packaging (via tool bundling mechanism)

The CLI is packaged as a .NET tool with:
```xml
<PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>
<ToolCommandName>monodreams</ToolCommandName>
```

This allows installation via `dotnet tool install MonoDreams.Cli` and the bundled registry to be accessed from anywhere.

---

### Summary: Key Architectural Insights

1. **No multi-platform support currently exists** — The CLI hardcodes `WinExe`, `net8.0`, and `MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` for all projects.

2. **Module manifests are stateless** — They contain only metadata; files are implicit (entire directory copied). This makes drift impossible by design.

3. **Installation is idempotent** — Files are overwritten, csproj edits use managed Labels to avoid duplication, MGCB edits check for markers.

4. **Dependency resolution is strict** — Cycles are rejected, missing modules cause errors, no optional dependencies.

5. **Templates are embedded** — No external template files; the CLI is fully self-contained and can be distributed as a single NuGet tool.

6. **Post-install notes are human+AI readable** — Markdown strings in manifests provide wiring instructions that both developers and AI agents can parse.

---

All file paths are absolute and ready for your web target planning phase.

**Manifest Structure** (required fields, then optional):

| Field | Type | Required | Purpose |
|-------|------|----------|---------|
| `name` | string (kebab-case) | YES | Module identifier, must match directory name |
| `description` | string (≤120 chars) | YES | One-line summary shown by `monodreams list` |
| `dependencies` | array of strings | NO | Other modules required (transitive); resolved at install time |
| `nugetDependencies` | array of objects | NO | NuGet packages to inject into user's .csproj |
| `csprojProperties` | object (key-value) | NO | MSBuild properties appended to csproj PropertyGroup |
| `files` | array of objects | NO | Override implicit file list (source/destination/kind mappings) |
| `mgcbEntries` | array of strings | NO | Lines appended to Content/Content.mgcb for content pipeline |
| `postInstallNotes` | string (markdown) | NO | Terminal output after install (wiring instructions) |
| `agentsMd` | string (path) | NO | Path to AGENTS.md snippet appended to user's project AGENTS.md |
| `premisesRef` | string (path) | NO | Reference to docs/premises.md for module invariants |
| `demo` | object | NO | Optional runnable demo (entry class, description, extra dependencies) |

**File Copy Convention:**
- By default, **every file** in `MonoDreams/<module>/` (except `module.json`) is copied to the user's project at the same relative path
- Namespaces are file-path independent in C#, so `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` → user's `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` with namespace `MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`
- If a module needs files from outside its directory, it explicitly lists them in `files[].source/destination`

**Module Directory Layout Example:**
```
MonoDreams/
├── module.schema.json       (JSON Schema for all manifests)
├── presets.json             (curated module combinations)
├── MODULES.md               (docs, this file)
├── MonoDreams.csproj        (engine project, references all modules via glob)
├── foundation/              (required base)
│   ├── module.json
│   ├── Screen/
│   │   ├── ScreenController.cs
│   │   └── IGameScreen.cs
│   ├── System/
│   ├── Component/
│   ├── Input/
│   ├── Hierarchy/
│   ├── Transform/
│   ├── Logger/
│   ├── Replay/
│   └── docs/
│       └── premises.md
├── rendering/
│   ├── module.json
│   ├── Draw/
│   ├── Camera/
│   ├── Culling/
│   ├── MasterRenderSystem.cs
│   └── ...
├── ui/
│   ├── module.json
│   ├── Layout/
│   │   ├── AutoLayoutSystem.cs
│   │   ├── AutoLayoutBuilder.cs
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── demo/                (excluded from core, included with --with-demo)
│   │   └── ...
│   └── ...
├── camera/
│   ├── module.json          (has demo field)
│   ├── Component/
```

**Example Manifest with Complex Wiring: `dialogue/module.json`**
```json
{
  "name": "dialogue",
  "description": "YarnSpinner dialogue with content pipeline importer...",
  "dependencies": ["rendering-text", "ui"],
  "nugetDependencies": [
    { "id": "YarnSpinner", "version": "3.0.2" },
    { "id": "YarnSpinner.Compiler", "version": "3.0.2" },
    { "id": "CsvHelper", "version": "31.0.4" }
  ],
  "csprojProperties": {
    "CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies": "true",
    "EnableDynamicLoading": "true",
    "GenerateRuntimeConfigurationFiles": "true"
  },
  "mgcbEntries": [
    "/importer:YarnSpinnerImporter",
    "/processor:YarnSpinnerProcessor"
  ],
  "postInstallNotes": "## dialogue installed\n\n**Content pipeline.** Your project DLL must be referenced by MGCB...",
  "premisesRef": "docs/premises.md"

```

---

### 3. How `monodreams add <module>` Works

**File:** `MonoDreams.Cli/Installer/Installer.cs`

**Step-by-step flow for `monodreams add rendering camera collision`:**

1. **Dependency Resolution** (`DependencyResolver.cs`):
   - Loads manifest for each requested module
   - Performs depth-first traversal of the dependency graph
   - Topologically sorts the result (dependencies first)
   - Skips any module already in `monodreams.json`
   - Result for above: `["rendering", "camera", "collision"]` (rendering must be installed before camera)

2. **File Enumeration** (`Installer.EnumerateFiles()`):
   - If manifest has explicit `files[]`, use that
   - Otherwise, walk `MonoDreams/<module>/` recursively, collecting all files except `module.json`
   - Determine `kind` (code, asset, tool) based on file extension
   - Return list of `FileEntry{source, destination, kind}`

3. **File Copy** (`Installer.Apply()`):
   ```csharp
   foreach (var file in EnumerateFiles(manifest))
   {
       var src = Path.Combine(registry.EngineRoot, file.Source);
       var dst = Path.Combine(projectDir, file.Destination);
       Directory.CreateDirectory(Path.GetDirectoryName(dst)!);
       File.Copy(src, dst, overwrite: true);
   }
   ```

4. **Csproj Editing** (`CsprojEditor.ApplyModule()`):
   - Loads user's `.csproj` as XDocument
   - If module has `nugetDependencies`, creates/gets `<ItemGroup Label="MonoDreams.Cli managed">` and adds `<PackageReference>` entries
   - If module has `csprojProperties`, creates/gets `<PropertyGroup Label="MonoDreams.Cli managed">` and adds properties
   - Saves modified XDocument back to disk

5. **MGCB Editing** (`MgcbEditor.ApplyModule()`):
   - If `Content/Content.mgcb` exists and module has `mgcbEntries`:
     - Appends a marker comment: `# --- <module-name> (managed by monodreams-cli) ---`
     - Appends each entry
   - Idempotent: checks for marker to avoid duplication

6. **State Update** (`StateFile.Save()`):
   - Appends module names to `monodreams.json` modules list
   - Updates `updatedAt` timestamp

**Key Design:** No circular dependencies allowed; resolver throws on cycle detection.

---

### 4. Search for Existing Platform/Target/Desktop/Web References

**Grep Results:**
```bash
grep -r "platform|target|desktop|web|wasm" /MonoDreams.Cli --include="*.cs" --include="*.json" --include="*.md"
# NO MATCHES
```

**However, there is one hardcoded platform decision:**

In `ProjectScaffolder.cs`:
```csharp
private static void WriteCsproj(string projectDir, string projectName)
{
    var path = Path.Combine(projectDir, $"{projectName}.csproj");
    File.WriteAllText(path, $"""
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>          // <-- Desktop-only
    <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework> // <-- No multi-target
    <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <PublishReadyToRun>false</PublishReadyToRun>
    <TieredCompilation>false</TieredCompilation>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
```

And in `foundation/module.json`:
```json
"nugetDependencies": [
  { "id": "MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL", "version": "3.8.4" }  // <-- Desktop GL
]
```

**Current State:**
- No notion of "target platform" anywhere in the manifest schema
- No flags or conditionals in CLI commands for platform selection
- All scaffolded projects are `WinExe` targeting `net8.0`
- Foundation hardcodes `MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` (desktop-only)

---

### 5. Project Templates and Scaffolding

**Template Generation:** All templates are **embedded in the CLI as strings** in `ProjectScaffolder.cs`

**Generated on `monodreams init`:**

1. **`.csproj` template** (lines 17–30 of ProjectScaffolder.cs):
   ```xml
   <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
     <PropertyGroup>
       <OutputType>WinExe</OutputType>
       <TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>
       <RollForward>Major</RollForward>
       <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
       <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
       <PublishReadyToRun>false</PublishReadyToRun>
       <TieredCompilation>false</TieredCompilation>
     </PropertyGroup>
   </Project>
   ```

2. **`Program.cs` template** (lines 33–70):
   ```csharp
   using Microsoft.Xna.Framework;
   using Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics;

   namespace {projectName};

   public class {projectName}Game : Game
   {
       private readonly GraphicsDeviceManager _graphics;

       public {projectName}Game()
       {
           _graphics = new GraphicsDeviceManager(this);
           IsMouseVisible = true;
       }

       protected override void Update(GameTime gameTime)
       {
           base.Update(gameTime);
       }

       protected override void Draw(GameTime gameTime)
       {
           GraphicsDevice.Clear(Color.CornflowerBlue);
           base.Draw(gameTime);
       }

       public static void Main()
       {
           using var game = new {projectName}Game();
           game.Run();
       }
   }
   ```

3. **`app.manifest`** (lines 73–82):
   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
   <assembly manifestVersion="1.0" xmlns="urn:schemas-microsoft-com:asm.v1">
     <assemblyIdentity version="1.0.0.0" name="MonoGame.App"/>
   </assembly>
   ```

4. **`.gitignore`** (lines 85–94):
   ```
   bin/
   obj/
   debug/
   *.user
   ```

**No external template files exist.** Everything is C# string literals in `ProjectScaffolder.cs`.

---

### 6. Module Dependency Graph

**13 modules total**, organized in a DAG:

```
foundation (root, no deps)
├── rendering
│   ├── rendering-text
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug (+ collision soft-coupling)
│   ├── level-ldtk (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui
│       └── dialogue (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision (+ physics soft-coupling)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

**Presets** (curated module combinations in `presets.json`):
- `ldtk-platformer` — full 2D platformer with LDtk levels, dialogue, UI
- `blender-platformer` — same but with Blender-exported levels
- `infinite-runner` — procedural runner (no level files, minimal UI)

---

### 7. State Tracking

**File:** `monodreams.json` (generated in project root after `init`)

```json
{
  "schema": "https://monodreams.dev/state.schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "modules": ["foundation", "rendering", "camera"],
  "createdAt": "2025-06-21T12:00:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2025-06-21T12:05:00Z"
}
```

This file is used by `add` to skip already-installed modules and prevent redundant copies.

---

### 8. Registry Loading

**File:** `Registry.cs`

The registry can come from three sources (in priority order):
1. **Explicit path:** `--registry <path>` flag
2. **Repo root:** If run from within the engine repo (detected by presence of `MonoDreams/` with `module.json` files)
3. **Bundled:** Embedded in the CLI tool during packaging (via tool bundling mechanism)

The CLI is packaged as a .NET tool with:
```xml
<PackAsTool>true</PackAsTool>
<ToolCommandName>monodreams</ToolCommandName>
```

This allows installation via `dotnet tool install MonoDreams.Cli` and the bundled registry to be accessed from anywhere.

---

### Summary: Key Architectural Insights

1. **No multi-platform support currently exists** — The CLI hardcodes `WinExe`, `net8.0`, and `MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` for all projects.

2. **Module manifests are stateless** — They contain only metadata; files are implicit (entire directory copied). This makes drift impossible by design.

3. **Installation is idempotent** — Files are overwritten, csproj edits use managed Labels to avoid duplication, MGCB edits check for markers.

4. **Dependency resolution is strict** — Cycles are rejected, missing modules cause errors, no optional dependencies.

5. **Templates are embedded** — No external template files; the CLI is fully self-contained and can be distributed as a single NuGet tool.

6. **Post-install notes are human+AI readable** — Markdown strings in manifests provide wiring instructions that both developers and AI agents can parse.

---

All file paths are absolute and ready for your web target planning phase.

KNI is a cross-platform C# game framework for creating games for desktop PCs, mobile devices, Virtual Reality headsets and the Web, using dotnet framework & the C# programming language. It is an open-source re-implementation of the discontinued Microsoft's XNA Framework.

## Overview

MonoGame itself does not officially support web or WebAssembly targets, but there is a solution available through the community.

## KNI as the Solution

## Shared Game Library Support

The library MonoGame.Framework is split into MonoGame.Framework, Xna.Framework.Content, Xna.Framework.Graphics, Xna.Framework.Audio, and Xna.Framework.Media, which allows for modular shared game library structures across different platform projects.

I now have a solid grounding in both KNI and the MonoDreams build/distribution model. Before I write the plan, the key facts:

- **KNI** = MonoGame-compatible fork; **same `Microsoft.Xna.Framework` namespace**, but **different assembly identities** (`nkast.Xna.Framework.*`). So MonoDreams' own source recompiles unchanged, but every *precompiled* third-party dep needs a KNI build.
- **MonoGame.Extended → `KNI.Extended`** exists on NuGet. **LDtkMonogame has no KNI build** (would need vendoring/recompiling). YarnSpinner/CsvHelper/DefaultEcs are pure .NET (fine; `DefaultParallelRunner(1)` is already single-threaded, good for WASM).
- **Web = BlazorGL** (WebGL/WASM, Blazor WebAssembly SDK, net8.0). Needs a Blazor host entry (not `Program.cs → game.Run()`), content rebuilt with KNI's MGCB (`/platform:BlazorGL`, KNIFX shaders), and likely `GraphicsProfile.Reach` (MonoDreams currently hardcodes `HiDef`).
- **Web breaks** MonoDreams' filesystem code: `Logger` file output, `GameSettings` save/load, `InputReplayPlan`, `BlenderLevelParserSystem` (reads JSON from disk), `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`, plus `AppDomain.BaseDirectory`/`Environment` usage.
- **CLI** currently hardcodes `WinExe`/`net8.0`/`DesktopGL`; no platform notion in manifests or scaffolder.

A few scoping decisions genuinely change the plan's shape. Let me get your direction on them.

KNI.Extended includes features for pipeline, bmfont, tiled, texture atlas, input, viewport, fps, shapes, and sprite functionality. To use the content pipeline extension, refer to the Setup MGCB Editor documentation.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding your query about KNI BlazorGL content pipeline, MGCB, platform builds, and custom content processors:

## Key Findings:

**BlazorGL Platform Support:**
You can edit .mgcb files by removing the '/Platform:BlazorGL' line, as the platform is actually specified from the .csproj during a build rather than being required inside the .mgcb file.

**KNI Content Pipeline Tools:**
The KNI SDK comes with its own PipelineEditor, which can be launched by typing 'KNI PipelineEditor' in the Start menu. The mgcb tool is the command line tool for content processing, while the pipeline-editor tool is a GUI frontend for content processing.

**Shader/Effect Processing:**
The 2MGFX tool was renamed to KniFXC. This appears to be the shader/effect compiler for KNI projects.

**Net8.0 Upgrade:**
The content editor was upgraded from net4.x to net8.

**Custom Content Processors:**
The search results show that MonoGame/KNI supports custom content processors through pipeline extension libraries. A content pipeline extension library is a .NET assembly that's referenced within a .mgcb file and then invoked by the MonoGame Content Builder, with the result being custom data getting encoded and stored in MonoGame's XNB format.

For more detailed information about custom content processor implementation and BlazorGL-specific configurations, you may want to check the KNI GitHub repository directly or their discussion forums.

# Enable Web Browser (KNI/BlazorGL) targeting for MonoDreams

## Context

MonoDreams currently builds for desktop only — every project references
`MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` 3.8.4, scaffolds `WinExe`/`net8.0`, and
the engine source freely touches the filesystem (`Logger`, `GameSettings`,
`InputReplayPlan`, `BlenderLevelParserSystem`, `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`,
`AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory`, env vars). The goal of this work is
to let MonoDreams devs build games that run in the browser (Chrome latest)
via **KNI's BlazorGL** backend, and to let a single game project be
**desktop-only, web-only, or multi-platform (desktop + web)**.

**Why KNI works as the path:** KNI is a MonoGame-compatible fork that keeps
the same `Microsoft.Xna.Framework` *namespace* but ships under different
*assembly identities* (`nkast.Xna.Framework.*`). Consequence: **MonoDreams'
own source recompiles unchanged** against either backend, but every
*precompiled* third-party dependency needs a KNI-built variant. The chosen
scope (confirmed with the user) is the maximal one:

- **Proof target:** the full LDtk platformer (`LoadLevelExampleGameScreen`)
  running in Chrome.
- **Project model:** shared game library + per-platform head projects.
- **CLI:** full automation — `monodreams init --platform desktop|web|multi`.
- **Web gaps:** vendor + recompile `LDtkMonogame` against KNI for full parity
  (no module left desktop-only).

## Confirmed external facts (KNI ecosystem)

| Concern | Desktop (today) | Web (KNI/BlazorGL) |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime framework | `MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` 3.8.4 | `nkast.Xna.Framework.Blazor` (+ split `nkast.Xna.Framework.*` pkgs), net8.0, **Blazor WebAssembly SDK** |
| MonoGame.Extended | `MonoGame.Extended` 4.1.0 | `KNI.Extended` (4/5/6.x) |
| Extended content pipeline | `MonoGame.Extended.Content.Pipeline` | `KNI.Extended.Content.Pipeline` |
| Content builder/MGCB | `MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task` 3.8.4 | `nkast.Xna.Framework.Content.Pipeline` + `…Builder.Windows` |
| Shaders | `.fx` via 2MGFX | `.fx` via **KniFXC** (KNIFX format) |
| LDtk | `LDtkMonogame` + `.ContentPipeline` 1.8.0 | **no KNI build → vendor & recompile** |
| YarnSpinner / CsvHelper / DefaultEcs | pure .NET | unchanged (pure .NET, no MonoGame ref) |

Key mechanics confirmed: the **same `.mgcb` builds for either platform** —
the platform is taken from the head csproj at build time, not hardcoded in
the `.mgcb`. Custom content processors (BitmapFont, LDtk, Yarn) run on the

## Context

MonoDreams currently builds for desktop only — every project references
`MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` 3.8.4, scaffolds `WinExe`/`net8.0`, and
the engine source freely touches the filesystem (`Logger`, `GameSettings`,
`InputReplayPlan`, `BlenderLevelParserSystem`, `ScreenshotCaptureSystem`,
`AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory`, env vars). The goal of this work is
to let MonoDreams devs build games that run in the browser (Chrome latest)
via **KNI's BlazorGL** backend, and to let a single game project be
**desktop-only, web-only, or multi-platform (desktop + web)**.

**Why KNI works as the path:** KNI is a MonoGame-compatible fork that keeps
the same `Microsoft.Xna.Framework` *namespace* but ships under different
*assembly identities* (`nkast.Xna.Framework.*`). Consequence: **MonoDreams'
own source recompiles unchanged** against either backend, but every
*precompiled* third-party dependency needs a KNI-built variant. The chosen
scope (confirmed with the user) is the maximal one:

- **Proof target:** the full LDtk platformer (`LoadLevelExampleGameScreen`)
  running in Chrome.
- **Project model:** shared game library + per-platform head projects.
- **CLI:** full automation — `monodreams init --platform desktop|web|multi`.
- **Web gaps:** vendor + recompile `LDtkMonogame` against KNI for full parity
  (no module left desktop-only).

| Runtime framework | `MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL` 3.8.4 | `nkast.Xna.Framework.Blazor` (+ split `nkast.Xna.Framework.*` pkgs), net8.0, **Blazor WebAssembly SDK** |

lookup, log sink) in `foundation`. Desktop implementation = real FS (current
behavior); web implementation = `Console`/in-memory/browser storage (and no-op
or blob-download for screenshots, no-op for replay-from-disk). Make
`GraphicsProfile` and window/headless setup platform-conditional in the heads.
Audit all 13 modules for other non-portable APIs (none found beyond the above
in exploration, but verify). **Read first:** `docs/CORE_TENETS.md` and the
`foundation`, `debug`, `level-blender` premises — `Logger`, replay, and
`ScreenController` invariants live there.

- **MonoGame.Extended → KNI.Extended:** map runtime + content-pipeline packages
  per platform (BitmapFont text rendering depends on this).
- **Vendor LDtkMonogame:** bring its runtime + content-pipeline (+ codegen if
  used) source into the repo (e.g. `MonoDreams/level-ldtk/vendor/`), built
  against the active backend via `$(MonoDreamsPlatform)`. Verify its license
  permits vendoring; pin the upstream version. This makes `level-ldtk`
  web-capable. **Read first:** `level-ldtk` premises.
- **Shaders:** port `MultiTextureEffect.fx` and `disabled_effect.fx` to KNIFX
  via `KniFXC`; confirm Reach-profile compatibility (a `.glsl` variant of
  `MultiTextureEffect` already exists — reuse/validate it).
- **Yarn importer:** confirm `MonoDreams/dialogue/YarnSpinnerImporter.cs` /
  `YarnSpinnerWriter.cs` compile against `nkast.Xna.Framework.Content.Pipeline`
  for the web content build. YarnSpinner/CsvHelper/DefaultEcs runtimes need no
  change.

### Phase 3 — Reference app to the shared-lib + heads layout (the proof)
Restructure `MonoDreams.Examples` into `…Examples.Core` + `…Examples.Desktop`
+ `…Examples.Web` (keep desktop green throughout). Set up per-platform content
builds:
- Desktop: existing `Content/Content.mgcb` via `MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task`.
- Web: same `.mgcb` via KNI's builder + `KNI.Extended.Content.Pipeline` +
  vendored LDtk pipeline + Yarn importer (KNI build), `/platform:BlazorGL`,

takes input in Chrome latest. This converted Examples layout doubles as the
source-of-truth template the CLI will generate. (`MonoDreams.Demos` can follow

  `Core` lib + `Desktop` head (`Program.cs → game.Run()`) + `Web` head (Blazor
  WASM SDK, `Index.razor`, `Program.cs` host builder, `wwwroot/index.html`
  canvas + runtime config) + `.sln`, driven by `--platform desktop|web|multi`.

  platform-aware — inject the right package per platform, set

- CLI: `MonoDreams.Cli/Installer/ProjectScaffolder.cs`, `CsprojEditor.cs`,

## Key risks
1. **HiDef shaders on BlazorGL** — WebGL/Reach may not support the current
   `MultiTextureEffect`; the Phase 0 spike + Phase 2 shader port must confirm
   the multi-texture path works in WebGL (fallback: a Reach-compatible variant).
2. **Vendored LDtk drift** — vendoring forks LDtkMonogame; needs a pinned
   version + note to re-sync on upstream changes (mitigated by it being source
   MonoDreams already controls shadcn-style).
3. **Content-build toolchain on macOS/Linux** — KNI's MGCB/KniFXC tooling
   availability off-Windows must be verified early (the CI/dev build host).
4. **Asset load over HTTP** — `BlenderLevelParserSystem` reads JSON from disk;
   on web, content must come through `ContentManager`/HTTP, not `File.*`
   (covered by the Phase 1 abstraction).

  single-head project; `monodreams add <module>` injects correct per-platform
  packages.

---
name: verifying-loadlevel-screen
description: How to run + screenshot MonoDreams.Examples LoadLevelExampleGameScreen (and the fresh-worktree build-order gotcha)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Capturing `LoadLevelExampleGameScreen` (the full LDtk/Blender platformer reference screen) for visual verification.

**Why:** Examples' `--headless` makes `Draw` early-return (1×1 backbuffer, renders nothing), so the CLAUDE.md screenshot path does NOT work for Examples — you must run **non-headless**. (This is the opposite of `MonoDreams.Demos`, whose headless mode renders full-res and is the documented self-verify path — see [[block-demo-pattern]].)

**How to apply:**
1. In a fresh worktree, build core FIRST or the Examples content build fails with `Failed to create importer 'YarnSpinnerImporter'`. Cause: the MGCB step references `MonoDreams/bin/$(Configuration)/net8.0/MonoDreams.dll` by absolute path, not as an MSBuild dependency, so it runs before the core dll exists. Fix: `dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj -c Debug` then `dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj -c Debug`. (Relevant to the KNI web content-pipeline phase — same fragility per platform.)
2. Set `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR=<some dir>`; write `<dir>/input_replay.json` with `"startLevel"` (`"Level_0"` = LDtk "Level 1"; `"Blender_Level"` = "Level 2", the elephant-kid scene), `"screenshots": true`, and a non-empty `"commands"` list (replay auto-exits when commands drain → game quits). Screenshot system captures every 2.0s.
3. Run `dotnet run --no-build -c Debug --project MonoDreams.Examples` (opens a real window on macOS; needs a GUI session). Debug's ImGui inspector is hidden by default (F1 toggles), so screenshots are clean. PNGs land in `MONODREAMS_DEBUG_DIR`.

Note for `Blender_Level`: a logged "content file was not found" from `LevelLoadRequestSystem` is EXPECTED/caught — it probes for a nonexistent `World/Blender_Level` LDtk level; the Blender parser handles the actual scene.

Observed current state (2026-06): Blender_Level renders correctly; Level_0 tilemap renders in the lower-right with the player spawning offset above/left of the geometry (possible camera/spawn positioning quirk, not yet investigated).

# MonoDreams Project Memory

## Project Structure (Post-Refactor)
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library with rendering, camera, cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific: screens, input, dialogue, layout, settings, entity factories
- `MonoDreams.YarnSpinner/` — isolated YarnSpinner integration (not referenced by core)
- Build: `dotnet build` for everything; individual projects can be built separately

## Key Architecture Decisions
- **EntityInfo** is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`), Examples has `EntityType` enum convenience
- **Namespace conflicts**: `MonoDreams.EntityFactory` (not `.Entity`) to avoid shadowing `DefaultEcs.Entity`
- **CameraFollowTarget** lives in `MonoDreams.Component` (not Camera subdir) to avoid conflict with `Camera` class
- Core has no implicit usings — always add `using System;`, `using System.Collections.Generic;`, `using System.Linq;` when moving files from Examples to core

## Refactoring Patterns
- When moving files: use `cp` + `sed` (not cat/heredoc) so user can cache permissions in Claude Code
- Always `sed -i ''` on macOS (BSD sed requires empty string for in-place editing)
- After moving files from Examples to core, check for empty directories and remove them
- Build after every phase to catch issues early
- The plan was organized into phases with commits per phase for bisectability

7 commits implementing the full core/Examples alignment refactoring.
